proof_skeleton_nl: Work in the localized congruence ring Loc_{M_n} with M_n(q)=[n]_q Φ_n(q)^2. First show that the clearing factor U_{d,n}(q)=∏_{j=1}^{n-1}(1+q^{dj}) is coprime to M_n(q), so U_{d,n}(q) is invertible in Loc_{M_n}. Independently, show that every denominator (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k occurring in the theorem sum is also invertible modulo M_n(q); therefore the original sum T_{d,r,n}(q) and the target term R_{d,r,n}(q) are legitimate elements of Loc_{M_n}. Next define the cleared difference G_{d,r,n}(q)=U_{d,n}(q)(T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q)) and use the denominator-clearing identity (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k=(q^d;q^d)_k(-q^d;q^d)_k to show that G_{d,r,n}(q) is a Laurent polynomial. The only theorem-specific input is then the bottleneck lemma asserting that G_{d,r,n}(q) is divisible by M_n(q) in Q[q,q^{-1}]. By the meaning of divisibility, write G_{d,r,n}(q)=M_n(q)H_{d,r,n}(q) with H_{d,r,n}(q) Laurent. Since T_{d,r,n}(q) and R_{d,r,n}(q) lie in Loc_{M_n} and U_{d,n}(q) is invertible there, the generic localization-cancellation lemma converts the cleared equality U_{d,n}(q)(T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q))=M_n(q)H_{d,r,n}(q) into the desired congruence T_{d,r,n}(q) ≡ R_{d,r,n}(q) mod M_n(q). Unfolding the definitions yields exactly the displayed theorem. This assembly deliberately avoids the previously rejected false special-value and root-of-unity sublemmas and fixes the ambient-ring issue from the start.

steps.derives: For admissible d,r,n, if M_n(q):=[n]_q Φ_n(q)^2 and U_{d,n}(q):=∏_{j=1}^{n-1}(1+q^{dj}), then gcd(U_{d,n}(q),M_n(q))=1 in Z[q].
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the conclusion of L1 after naming M_n(q).

steps.derives: For admissible d,r,n, the rational functions T_{d,r,n}(q)=Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2}/(q^{2d};q^{2d})_k and R_{d,r,n}(q):=[rn]_q q^{r(1-n)/2} belong to the localization Loc_{M_n}.
steps.trivial_justification: L2 states precisely that each summand of T_{d,r,n}(q), the whole sum T_{d,r,n}(q), and the target term R_{d,r,n}(q) lie in Loc_{M_n}.

steps.derives: Define G_{d,r,n}(q):=U_{d,n}(q)(T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q)). Then G_{d,r,n}(q) belongs to Z[q,q^{-1}].
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the cleared-polynomial statement of L3.

steps.derives: The Laurent polynomial G_{d,r,n}(q) is divisible by M_n(q)=[n]_q Φ_n(q)^2 in Q[q,q^{-1}].
steps.trivial_justification: This is precisely the bottleneck divisibility claim supplied by L4.

steps.derives: There exists H_{d,r,n}(q) in Q[q,q^{-1}] such that G_{d,r,n}(q)=M_n(q) H_{d,r,n}(q) in Q(q).
steps.trivial_justification: By definition, divisibility of G_{d,r,n}(q) by M_n(q) in Q[q,q^{-1}] means exactly that such a Laurent polynomial H_{d,r,n}(q) exists.

steps.derives: In the localized-congruence sense, T_{d,r,n}(q) ≡ R_{d,r,n}(q) mod M_n(q), where M_n(q)=[n]_q Φ_n(q)^2.
steps.trivial_justification: From A3 and A5 we have U_{d,n}(q)(T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q))=M_n(q)H_{d,r,n}(q) in Q(q), with H_{d,r,n}(q) Laurent. From A2 both T_{d,r,n}(q) and R_{d,r,n}(q) lie in Loc_{M_n}. From A1 the polynomial U_{d,n}(q) is coprime to M_n(q). Therefore all hypotheses of L5 hold with X=T_{d,r,n}, Y=R_{d,r,n}, U=U_{d,n}, and M=M_n. Applying L5 yields T_{d,r,n}(q) ≡ R_{d,r,n}(q) mod M_n(q).

steps.derives: Let [m]_q = (1−q^m)/(1−q), let (a;q)_k = ∏_{j=0}^{k−1} (1−aq^j), let (a,b,c;q)_k = (a;q)_k (b;q)_k (c;q)_k, and let Φ_n(q) be the nth cyclotomic polynomial. Prove that for positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r)=1 and r ≤ d, and for every integer n > 1 with n ≡ 1 mod 2d, we have Σ_{k=0}^{n−1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^(k(d−dk−2r)/2) / (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k ≡ [rn]_q q^(r(1−n)/2) mod [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2.
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly A6 after unfolding the definitions of T_{d,r,n}(q), R_{d,r,n}(q), and M_n(q), together with the standing notation for q-integers, q-shifted factorials, and congruence modulo M_n(q).
